ItemGenerationAndUsage.MHA Items:
## MHA ITEMS
- Currency is yen. Prices: an onigiri about 150, a cafeteria lunch 500-800, a train ride 200-400; part-time work pays about 1,100 an hour; licensed support gear costs tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands. The school or agency pays for hero costumes. A U.A. student's costume is always the item "Student hero costume" (a later redesign is "Second hero costume"); "Agency hero costume" belongs only to licensed pros, sidekicks and faculty.
- Use the world's categories: Armor (outfits and costumes), Weapon, Support Gear, Tool, Consumable, Accessory. No magic: everything is technology, medicine or matter a Quirk made.
- Inventory: add an item only when it physically enters the character's possession (bought after a stated price is paid, given, found, built, returned); remove it when it is used up, handed over, broken beyond use, stolen, lost or confiscated. Seeing, discussing or being offered an item changes nothing. Paying: every payment subtracts its amount from Yen when it is paid, whether an item comes now or later (an order, a deposit, a fee, a fare, a meal); a sale removes the item and adds the price; nothing is free unless it is a gift. Nobody pays more Yen than they carry.
- Support gear is built for one user's Quirk or needs, by U.A.'s Development Studio under Power Loader, a support company or a back-alley maker. It aims, amplifies, protects or supplies; it never grants a Quirk or a Quirk effect the user lacks. It has charge, ammunition, durability and legal limits, and a broken device stays broken until its maker repairs it. Costume changes go through the school or agency and take days.
- Licensing: hero costumes and support gear are licensed items. Carrying weapons or Quirk gear in public without a license is a crime; police seize it, and faculty confiscate dangerous gear on campus.
- Medical: first aid stabilizes, bandages and splints; it does not mend bones or replace a doctor. Each treatment uses one First aid kit from the stack (quantity minus one), not the whole stack.
- Illegal goods: black-market gear, forged IDs and Quirk-boosting drugs such as Trigger are rare, dangerous and a crime to hold; Trigger costs the user self-control and health. Items tied to later canon events appear only once the story reaches them.
- A new item states what it is, who made it, its limits and a plausible price, in the world's format: description, then "[ Category | price or source ]". Never invent combat properties from a name.
- Anything given to a child (Eri, Kota Izumi or anyone of the Child type) is a child's thing and child-safe.
ItemGenerationAndUsage.MHA Items Kept:
## ITEMS THE PLAYER KEEPS
- Remove an item only when the player's own action gives, sells, uses up, breaks or loses it, or someone takes it in a scene the player sees. The character never drops, forgets or leaves an item behind on the narrator's own account.
- Crafting and building: the materials are used up only in the same update that adds the finished item; if the work fails or stops, the materials stay with the player.
- Nobody keeps the player's items or materials: anything handed over for a job, a repair or a look comes back unless the player gave or sold it.
ItemGenerationAndUsage.MHA Shops, Prices and Supply:
## MHA SHOPS, PRICES AND SUPPLY

## WHERE THINGS COME FROM
- Convenience stores, open all night at every station exit and on most blocks: onigiri, bento boxes, canned coffee, energy drinks, protein bars, bandages, umbrellas and phone chargers. Vending machines on every block sell canned drinks.
- Drugstores: first aid kits, painkillers, burn gel, ice packs and splints.
- Kiyashi Shopping Mall and city shopping streets: clothes for every body type, backpacks, sports gear, grip gloves, climbing rope, fitness trackers, phones, laptops and tablets.
- The Hero Merch Arcade at Musutafu Station's south exit: figures, trading cards and replica costumes. A replica is a toy or a costume piece with no protection and no gear function.
- Shrines: omamori charms.
- Hero costumes and licensed support gear never sell over a shop counter. Students get theirs through U.A.'s costume request system and the Development Studio; licensed heroes and agencies order from support companies with registration papers, and delivery takes days.
- Police and agencies issue items and never sell them: handcuffs, riot shields, police tactical vests, agency radios, agency phones, hero licenses.
- Brokers such as Giran sell what the law forbids: unregistered gear and weapons, forged IDs, lockpick sets, burner phones and Trigger vials, at a markup and only to buyers someone vouches for. The sale itself is a crime for both sides.

## PRICES
- A listed world item costs what its own description says. A new item is priced by its class: snacks and drinks 100-300 yen, meals 500-1,500, clothes several thousand to tens of thousands, electronics tens of thousands, registered gear tens to hundreds of thousands, black-market goods well above their legal price.
- Paying with an IC transit card or a smartphone still subtracts the amount from Yen; the card and the phone stay in the inventory.
- Lunch Rush's set meals are paid at the cafeteria counter like any other meal. Recovery Girl's gummies are free.

## INCOME
- Yen arrives only when the story hands it over: wages at the end of a shift or on payday, a broker's fee after a job, an agency salary, money from family, a refund, a sale. School lessons and exercises pay nothing.
- People a hero saves do not pay them; a grateful shopkeeper may give food, which is a gift item.
- Money or property found in the street belongs to its owner. Japanese custom and law say it goes to the nearest police box; keeping it is a crime.

## ISSUED ITEMS
- Issued items enter the inventory at the moment of handover and cost no Yen: a student ID, uniforms and textbooks at enrollment, a student hero costume on the day the cases are handed out, an agency radio on hiring, a provisional or full hero license when the Commission issues it.
- Leaving a job returns that employer's issued items. A revoked license is removed.
ItemGenerationAndUsage.MHA Inventory Cases:
## MHA INVENTORY CASES

## USE THE WORLD'S ITEM NAMES
When something in the story is a world item, use that item's exact name so it stacks with what the character already holds and keeps its bonuses: a medkit is a First aid kit, a roll of tape for binding villains is Capture tape, cuffs are Handcuffs, a rice ball is an Onigiri, a lunch box is a Bento box, a phone is a Smartphone, a train card is an IC transit card, a fuel pouch is a Quirk fuel pack. Make a new item only when no world item fits.

## WHAT USE REMOVES
- Consumables leave one at a time: eating removes one Onigiri or Bento box; binding one person removes one Capture tape or one Zip ties; each throw removes one Smoke grenade or Flashbang; each Finite Fuel top-up removes one Quirk fuel pack; dressing one wound removes one Bandages.
- Durable items stay through ordinary use: a smartphone, a capture weapon, a costume, gloves, goggles, a bag. Damage that leaves them working changes nothing in the inventory.
- A costume or outfit changed out of stays in the inventory; changing clothes moves nothing in or out.

## SEIZED, CONFISCATED, RETURNED
- Police seize illegal weapons, black-market gear, forged IDs and Trigger as evidence: remove them, and they never come back. Legal belongings taken at an arrest return on release.
- A teacher who confiscates gear on campus says when it comes back (after class, after a talk with Power Loader, at the end of term); it returns then, not before.

## NOT LOOT
- A defeated opponent's weapons, gear and cash go to the police as evidence. A hero, student or civilian who pockets them commits theft. A villain who strips a rival or a victim takes the item and the risk of being traced through it.
- Nothing appears from a fallen opponent that the story did not show them carrying.

## NEW ITEM DEFINITIONS
- Category follows use: a worn outfit is Armor; equipped Quirk or hero equipment is Support Gear; a held weapon is Weapon; a small worn piece is Accessory; carried kit is Tool; anything used up is Consumable.
- A Support Course build is one item made by its builder: it states the Quirk or need it serves, what it does, what makes it fail (charge, heat, ammunition, a jam) and that Power Loader signed it off or that it has not been signed off.
- Gear made for one person's Quirk works properly only for that person; anyone else gets its plain physical use.
- A gift between people names who gave it in its description when that matters to the story (a classmate's handmade charm, a family member's bento).
ItemGenerationAndUsage.MHA World-Settled Items:
## WORLD-SETTLED ITEMS
- A licensed support-gear order is settled by the world: when the character orders support gear, take no Yen and add no item. A courier delivers it days later and the world adds it then; never add the delivered gear a second time.
- After an arrest the world itself removes the weapons and contraband the police seize; remove nothing for the seizure.
- Purchases of listed items at the Campus Store, Convenience Store Corner, All-Night Convenience Store, Black Market Basement, Giran's Chinatown Office or a vending machine are settled by the world: take no Yen and add no item for them.
- License cards come only from the world: the Provisional hero license after the license exam, the Hero license at graduation or with a license Path. Never add, upgrade or swap a license card yourself.
- Asking about stock, prices or what a shop sells buys nothing: add or charge only what the player clearly asks to buy.
- Pay only the price agreed in the story: never take more Yen than the amount named in the scene. If the character's Yen does not cover it, the purchase fails: take no Yen and add no item.
